item.title: Re: BIONICLE
item.content:encoded: That's true. Dark Hunters like Roodaka, Nidhiki, and the Piraka always seemed more interesting and generally cooler - both as characters and as toys - to me than Makuta. Nidhiki was actually my favorite set until I got Vezon & Fenrakk.

item.title: Re: BIONICLE
item.content:encoded:
I vaguely remember Makuta in the second movie being too campy for me to take seriously. Roodaka scared the living daylights out of me as a kid though, especially in the scene where she's talking to Vakama about how loyal her horde is. She straight-up tells a bunch of visorak to jump off a tower and they immediately do just that and that scarred me a bit as a kid.

they were all far better than any toy-inspired direct-to-video animated movie has any right to be.

This. They had visorak blink independently and even had a janitor visorak cleaning the floor in the foreground of one of the scenes. It's insane how well-animated the movies are for that time.

item.title: Re: BIONICLE
item.content:encoded: My favorite was probably the second, but they were all far better than any toy-inspired direct-to-video animated movie has any right to be.

item.title: Re: BIONICLE
item.content:encoded:
I got Roodaka and Sidorak for my birthday this year! Those where the last ones I needed to complete the whole 2004-2005 Metru Nui set. She’s currently disassembled and combined with Keetongu to make the Shadowed One.

I haven’t played that, but I do have it for the gameboy advance or Nintendo DS I think. I had some other gameboy advance game where you play as the toa mata/nuva as well.

item.title: Re: BIONICLE
item.content:encoded:
I remember getting Roodaka and being so stoked at how many parts she had, so I could make more beautiful creations. I also watched one of the moves, but never got too terrible into the lore.

I remember the Bionicle movies being unusually good for the time—especially the third movie, Web of Shadows. Roodaka's voice actor did an amazing job as the Queen of the Visorak. The other two movies were alright; though not as memorable as the third I felt.

item.title: Re: BIONICLE
item.content:encoded:
I would make the sets, them immediately destroy them and add their pieces to my big box o' parts, from which I would build horrid amalgamations. I remember getting Roodaka and being so stoked at how many parts she had, so I could make more beautiful creations. I also watched one of the moves, but never got too terrible into the lore.

Also, did anyone else play Bionicle Heroes for PS2 or did I just dream that that game existed? I remember it being pretty chill.

item.title: BIONICLE
item.content:encoded:
This seems like as good a place as any to talk about my favorite toy line, and not just because I'm working on a skip related to it. So, are you a fan? What are your favorite sets?

Edit: This purpose of this thread is partially to get a feel for how many Bionicle fans we have on the site, so I can get an idea of how big a target audience the aforementioned skip would have.
